sandbox_start_desc: Starts a real WordPress + MariaDB stack on your machine (via Docker) and registers it as a site. It behaves like a production host, so backup and restore run through the real pipeline over SSH and restic.
sandbox_backup_desc: Create a restic backup of the sandbox site (files + database). This is your safety net for the drill.
sandbox_drill_desc: Practice a real recovery. This deliberately destroys the sandbox site: it replaces index.php with a "site is down" page, removes the wp-includes and uploads directories, and drops and recreates the WordPress database. The site can be fully recovered only by restoring a backup.
sandbox_drill_ack: I understand — I want to intentionally break this site for testing purposes. Its files and database will be corrupted, and it can be fully recovered only from a backup.
sandbox_drill_hint: Testing purpose: confirms your backup can recover a full site after a destructive change. Restore afterwards and the site should be identical to before.
sandbox_drill_no_backup: Take a backup first — the break drill is only enabled once at least one backup exists.
sandbox_broken_note: The sandbox site has been broken on purpose: index.php replaced, wp-includes and uploads removed, database dropped. Restore it from a backup below.
sandbox_broken_msg: The sandbox site is currently broken (disaster drill in progress). Restore it from the backup below.
sandbox_break_confirm_msg: This intentionally destroys the site (core files, uploads, front page and the whole database) for testing backup & restore. wp-config.php is kept so recovery works. Continue?
sandbox_restore_desc: Restore the files and database from the selected backup snapshot.
sandbox_restore_note_done: Restore completed — the site should now be identical to the selected backup snapshot.
sandbox_stop_desc: Tears down the local sandbox containers. Site record and backup history are kept.
sandbox_stop_confirm_msg: Stop and destroy the sandbox containers? The site record and its backups are kept.
sandbox_delete_desc: Permanently removes the test site: stops the sandbox containers, deletes the site record with all its backups from the database and wipes the sandbox data directory.
sandbox_delete_confirm_msg: This permanently deletes the sandbox site, all of its backups and the sandbox data. This cannot be undone.
